notes: Sleep disruption impairs consolidation and increases inflammation

key_citation: Savard & Morin, 2001; Garland et al., 2014; Irwin, 2015
notes: Highest evidence clinical pathway. Contains LOOP_02 (Depression↔Sleep) and LOOP_03 (Anxiety↔Sleep). Drives glymphatic clearance. Target of CBT-I, sleep hygiene, bright light therapy.

key_citation: Bower, 2014; Berger et al., 2015; Mustian et al., 2017
notes: Contains LOOP_01 (Fatigue↔Activity, gain=0.16, strongest feedback loop). Inflammation → fatigue → inactivity → deconditioning → reduced cerebral perfusion → cognition. Target of exercise interventions.

key_citation: Berman et al., 2014; Andreotti et al., 2015
notes: CAL covariance structure links subjective cognitive complaints with depression (reporting bias). PHQ-9 somatic confound warning during active treatment. Target of MBSR, psychoeducation.

key_citation: Simo et al., 2015; Mandelblatt et al., 2014
notes: Links metabolic comorbidities to cognitive outcomes via cerebral perfusion. Overlaps with M13 (Metabolic) and M11 (Cerebrovascular) mechanistic pathways. Target of diet and exercise.

key_citation: Kuiper et al., 2016; Fratiglioni et al., 2004
notes: Fatigue/depression → social withdrawal → reduced cognitive stimulation → verbal/executive decline. Fewest edges (3). Target of social support groups and psychoeducation.

key_citation: Felger et al., 2020, Mol Psychiatry; Bower, 2014, Brain Behav Immun
notes: Most robustly supported CRCI mechanism. Shared with OIC composite (M1+M2+M6) and NIC covariance (M3+M1).

key_citation: Joshi et al., 2010, Free Radic Biol Med; Conklin, 2004
notes: Component of OIC composite. ROS → lipid peroxidation → neuronal membrane damage. Feeds forward into DNA damage (M7).

key_citation: Bower et al., 2005; Sephton et al., 2013; Tell et al., 2014
notes: NIC covariance with M1. Cortisol slope primary proxy. Hippocampal glucocorticoid receptor-mediated memory impairment. Part of LOOP_05.

key_citation: Szuhany et al., 2015, J Psychiatr Res; Northey et al., 2019
notes: Primary exercise → cognition pathway. PLASMA BDNF only (not serum). SE 1.5x in cancer-specific contexts per paper. APOE e4 moderates (Grade A).

key_citation: van Praag et al., 1999; Erickson et al., 2011, PNAS
notes: Hippocampus-specific. BDNF-dependent. Age-moderated (declines with age). Primary evidence from animal models; human translational evidence emerging.

key_citation: Lomeli et al., 2017; Magistretti & Allaman, 2018
notes: Component of OIC composite. ATP depletion → reduced neuronal energy → processing speed deficits. No direct peripheral proxy for CNS mitochondrial function.

key_citation: Kuo et al., 2006; Acharya et al., 2016, Sci Rep
notes: Direct chemotherapy/radiation mechanism. Feeds into senescence (M9) via persistent damage foci. γ-H2AX is high-validity proxy.

key_citation: Cryan & Dinan, 2012; Jordan et al., 2018
notes: Emerging evidence. Chemo → dysbiosis → intestinal permeability → systemic inflammation → neuroinflammation. Converges on OIC. Shannon diversity is low-validity proxy.

key_citation: Sanoff et al., 2014; Demaria et al., 2017
notes: Chemotherapy-induced senescence → SASP → chronic inflammation. Links to ACC factor in temporal model. p16 is high-validity proxy.

key_citation: Xie et al., 2013, Science; Jessen et al., 2015
notes: Sleep-dependent CNS waste clearance. Part of LOOP_05 (HPA→Sleep→Glymphatic→Neuroinflammation→HPA). No direct peripheral proxy. Inferred from sleep + neuroinflammation trajectory.

key_citation: Kesler et al., 2017 (fMRI evidence)
notes: EDGELESS PLACEHOLDER. Conceptual pathway without parameterized edges in v1. Would require TCD/MRI perfusion data. Future expansion candidate.

key_citation: Kober et al., 2020; Lengacher et al., 2014 (methylation)
notes: Chemotherapy-induced methylation changes → altered gene expression in neuronal/glial cells. Modulates other pathways (OIC, neuroplasticity). No validated CNS peripheral proxy.

key_citation: Simo et al., 2015; Cheke et al., 2017
notes: Insulin resistance → impaired cerebral glucose metabolism → neuroinflammation. Dexamethasone and hormonal therapy exacerbate. Links to C4 (Vascular/metabolic clinical pathway).

key_citation: Wardill et al., 2016; Schroyen et al., 2021
notes: EDGELESS PLACEHOLDER. BBB permeability allows peripheral inflammatory mediators into CNS. NfL candidate proxy but cannot distinguish CNS from PNS damage.

key_citation: Bhatt et al., 2020; Gibson & Bhatt, 2018
notes: CONVERGENT HUB receiving from multiple mechanistic pathways. Final common pathway before cognitive domains. LTP/LTD, synaptic pruning, neurotransmitter balance. No direct peripheral proxy.

key_citation: Dietrich et al., 2006; Han et al., 2008; Deprez et al., 2012
notes: Chemo directly toxic to oligodendrocyte precursors → demyelination → white matter tract disruption. Primary effect on processing speed. DTI fractional anisotropy is gold standard (imaging, not peripheral).

key_citation: Saligan et al., 2015; Capuron et al., 2012
notes: Chemo may disrupt dopamine synthesis → reduced motivation → reduced engagement → secondary cognitive effects. Links to self-efficacy (L1) and fatigue (L4). Mostly animal model evidence.
